metadata.title: Customize the editor — Gazetta
metadata.description: Custom editor and field mount contracts, embedded forms, admin CSS themes and token overrides.

components.name: docs-customize-editor-body
components.content:
> These docs describe Gazetta's `main` branch. The latest release on npm, 0.8.0, is older and works differently in places, and it lacks security fixes made since. To follow these docs, [run Gazetta from `main`](https://github.com/gazetta-studio/gazetta-studio#quick-start). # Customize the editor Replace a template's editing form, add individual field widgets or theme the admin. These customizations live under the project's `admin/` directory and are shared across its sites. Template rendering is covered in [Templates](/docs/templates). ## Custom editors The CMS auto-generates forms from template schemas using @rjsf. You can replace the default form with a custom editor for any template. ### Create a custom editor Create `admin/editors/{template-name}.tsx`, exporting an `EditorMount` as the default export. Editors are separate project-level files, not exports from the template module. Lookup also accepts `{template-name}.ts`. For the `hero` template: ```tsx // admin/editors/hero.tsx import React, { useState } from 'react' import { createRoot, type Root } from 'react-dom/client' import { DefaultEditorForm } from 'gazetta/editor' import type { EditorMount } from 'gazetta/types' type EditorProps = Parameters[1] function HeroEditor(props: EditorProps) { const [data, setData] = useState(props.content) const handleChange = (c: Record) => { setData(c); props.onChange(c) } return (
{/* Your custom preview */}

{(data.title as string) || 'Untitled'}

{typeof data.subtitle === 'string' && data.subtitle &&

{data.subtitle}

}
{/* Default form for the fields. Forward every prop so custom fields (fieldsBaseUrl) and the asset picker (onPickAsset) keep working inside it. */}
) } const roots = new WeakMap() const editor: EditorMount = { mount(el, props) { // mount() runs once per mount cycle; content updates flow through // onChange and the editor's own state. const root = createRoot(el) roots.set(el, root) root.render() }, unmount(el) { roots.get(el)?.unmount(); roots.delete(el) }, } export default editor ``` The custom editor loads automatically when you select a hero component in the CMS. Templates without a custom editor use the default auto-generated form. ### What custom editors receive | Prop | Type | Description | |------|------|-------------| | `content` | `Record` | Current content values | | `schema` | `Record` | JSON Schema for the template | | `theme` | `'dark' \| 'light'` | Admin theme at mount time | | `fieldsBaseUrl` | `string` (optional) | Base URL for loading custom field modules | | `onPickAsset` | `(options) => Promise<{ _asset: string } \| null>` (optional) | Opens the asset picker; resolves on confirm, `null` on cancel | | `assetsApiBase` | `string` (optional) | Admin API base URL for asset-summary fetches | | `onChange` | `(content) => void` | Call when content changes | Forward all mount props to `DefaultEditorForm`, including `fieldsBaseUrl`, `onPickAsset` and `assetsApiBase`. Without the first two, custom fields render "No fields base URL configured" and asset fields can't open the picker; `assetsApiBase` lets asset fields fetch summaries from the correct API base. `theme` is the admin theme when the editor mounted; a theme switch doesn't remount it, so follow switches with the CSS tokens, not the prop. ### Embedding the default form Import `DefaultEditorForm` from `gazetta/editor` to embed the auto-generated form inside your custom editor, with custom UI above the standard form fields. ## Custom fields Custom fields are reusable widgets that replace individual form fields inside the default @rjsf form. Unlike custom editors (which replace the entire form), custom fields target a single property. ### Create a custom field Create `admin/fields/{field-name}.tsx`: ```tsx // admin/fields/brand-color.tsx import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react' import { createRoot, type Root } from 'react-dom/client' import type { FieldMount } from 'gazetta/types' const PRESETS = [ { label: 'Indigo', value: '#667eea' }, { label: 'Purple', value: '#764ba2' }, { label: 'Coral', value: '#f97066' }, ] function BrandColorPicker({ value, onChange }: { value: string; theme: 'dark' | 'light'; onChange: (v: string) => void }) { const [color, setColor] = useState(value || '#667eea') // The form calls mount() again with the new value on each change, so // the prop updates under a reused root - sync on undo/redo, revert // and draft restores. useEffect(() => { setColor(value || '#667eea') }, [value]) const handleChange = (v: string) => { setColor(v); onChange(v) } return (
{PRESETS.map(p => (
handleChange(e.target.value)} />
) } const roots = new WeakMap() const brandColor: FieldMount = { mount(el, { value, theme, onChange }) { // mount() runs again on value changes; reuse the root. let root = roots.get(el) if (!root) { root = createRoot(el) roots.set(el, root) } root.render() }, unmount(el) { roots.get(el)?.unmount(); roots.delete(el) }, } export default brandColor ``` ### Reference a custom field in a template schema Use `format.field('field-name')` in the Zod schema: ```ts // templates/banner/index.ts import { z } from 'zod' import { format, type TemplateFunction } from 'gazetta' export const schema = z.object({ heading: z.string().describe('Banner heading'), background: z.string().meta(format.field('brand-color')).describe('Background color'), }) type Content = z.infer const template: TemplateFunction = ({ content }) => ({ html: `

${(content?.heading ?? '').replace(/[&<>"']/g, char => `&#${char.charCodeAt(0)};`)}

`, css: '', js: '', }) export default template ``` This minimal render example leaves `background` unused; the custom widget still edits that value in the form. The `brand-color` field widget loads automatically when editing a component that uses the `banner` template. Other fields in the schema use the default form inputs. Custom fields apply to top-level schema properties only today - a property inside a nested `z.object(...)` or a `z.array(...)` item keeps the default input. ### What custom fields receive | Prop | Type | Description | |------|------|-------------| | `value` | `unknown` | Current field value | | `schema` | `Record` | JSON Schema for this property | | `theme` | `'dark' \| 'light'` | Theme on initial mount and later value updates (see below) | | `onChange` | `(value) => void` | Call when the value changes | The field receives `theme` at its initial mount and on later value updates. A theme switch alone does not call `mount` again; the default is `'dark'` when the form has no theme. To follow switches immediately, style with CSS tokens (`var(--color-*)` or your own) instead of branching on the prop. ### Custom fields + custom editors - **No custom editor** - custom fields work inside the default @rjsf form - **Custom editor with `DefaultEditorForm`** - custom fields work inside the embedded form - **Custom editor without `DefaultEditorForm`** - custom fields are NOT used (the custom editor controls everything) ## Customize admin appearance If your project has a file at `admin/theme.css`, Gazetta loads it after the admin's own styles, so at equal specificity your declarations win. Use it to: **Override Gazetta's tokens** - change brand color, status colors, radii, etc. ```css /* admin/theme.css */ :root { --color-primary: #6d28d9; --color-on-primary: #ffffff; --color-env-prod-bg: #fff5e6; } .dark { --color-primary: #a78bfa; --color-on-primary: #1e0b3b; --color-env-prod-bg: #3a2a10; } ``` A `:root`-only override applies in both themes - the light `--color-env-prod-bg` above would sit behind dark-mode text without its `.dark` counterpart. Keep each colour readable against what it sits on: text on `--color-bg`, and `--color-on-` text on a `--color-` fill. **Define custom tokens for custom editors and fields** - pick a prefix you own: ```css /* admin/theme.css */ :root { --myapp-json-key: #6366f1; --myapp-json-string: #10b981; } .dark { --myapp-json-key: #a5b4fc; --myapp-json-string: #4ade80; } ``` Your custom editor consumes via `var(--myapp-json-key)`. `theme.css` is appended after the app mounts; the admin doesn't wait for it to load, so first paint can precede it. ### Tokens you can override All of these have a light value on `:root` and, where it differs, a dark value on `.dark`. | Token | Purpose | |---|---| | `--color-primary` / `--color-on-primary` | Brand accent (primary buttons, links, active states) and text on it | | `--color-bg` / `--color-fg` / `--color-muted` | Page and panel background, text, secondary text | | `--color-border` / `--color-hover-bg` | Borders and dividers; hovered rows and quiet buttons | | `--color-input-bg` / `--color-input-border` | Text fields, selects, checkboxes | | `--color-bg-chip` / `--color-bg-code` | Chips and badges; code and JSON blocks | | `--color-accent` | Selected component in the component tree | | `--color-danger` / `--color-success` / `--color-warn` / `--color-info` | Severity fills and text (buttons, badges, status icons), each with `--color-on-danger` etc. for text on the fill | | `--color-danger-bg` / `--color-danger-fg` | Error banners (likewise `success`, `warning`, `info`) | | `--color-env-prod-bg` / `--color-env-prod-fg` | Production target badge (likewise `staging`) | | `--color-change-added` / `--color-change-modified` / `--color-change-deleted` | Change marks in the publish panel | | `--color-focus-ring`, `--focus-ring-width`, `--focus-ring-offset` | Keyboard focus outline | | `--color-overlay`, `--shadow-overlay` | Dialog backdrop; shadow of dialogs and menus | | `--radius-xs` / `--radius-sm` / `--radius-md` / `--radius-full` | Corner radii | | `--font-mono` | Monospace text | ### Reserved prefixes | Prefix | Owner | What you can do | |---|---|---| | `--color-*`, `--radius-*`, `--focus-ring-*`, `--shadow-*`, `--font-*` | Gazetta | Override existing - don't add new | | Anything else | You | Pick a prefix you own (`--myapp-*`, `--mycorp-*`) | ### Migrating from `--p-*` tokens Earlier versions of the admin were built on PrimeVue, and `admin/theme.css` overrode its `--p-*` tokens (for example `--p-primary-color`). The admin no longer uses PrimeVue, so those overrides have no effect: rename them to the `--color-*` token with the same purpose (`--p-primary-color` becomes `--color-primary`). --- [Edit this page on GitHub](https://github.com/gazetta-studio/gazetta-studio/edit/main/docs/customize-editor.md)
